nodes.label: Node CSV Format
nodes.rationale: Requires only id and kinds columns; auto-detected by column headers so node and edge CSVs can be mixed on stdin without flags. Additional columns become node properties.

nodes.label: Edge CSV Format
nodes.rationale: Requires start, end, and kind columns; auto-detected by headers. Additional columns become edge properties.

nodes.label: graphify-to-OpenGraph Converter
nodes.rationale: Deliberately schema-tolerant: accepts edges under links or edges, the {"graph": {...}} wrapper, and field-name variants (src/dst, name-as-id, cluster, weight, object-valued endpoints) so graph.json converts directly with no intermediate CSV.

nodes.label: Single Classified Kind per Node
nodes.rationale: Emitting exactly one classified kind is deliberate: gopengraph appends the import-wide source_kind to every node on export, so each node ends up with at most two kinds — within the cap that cogs enforces — letting graphify output merge cleanly with other sources.

nodes.label: source_kind Import Tag
nodes.rationale: Folded into every node's kinds and recorded in metadata so the whole import can be filtered or deleted as a unit in BloodHound.

nodes.label: match_by id Edge Endpoint Resolution
nodes.rationale: All edges use match_by: "id" so endpoints reference nodes by their ID field rather than by name lookup.

nodes.label: include Confidence Filter
nodes.rationale: No edges are dropped during conversion: low-confidence edges are kept with include: false (the filter passes EXTRACTED, or INFERRED with confidence_score >= 0.85), preserving the full graph while letting consumers filter.

nodes.label: Colon-to-Underscore ID Sanitization
nodes.rationale: Colons in graphify node ids are replaced with underscores because BloodHound does not support colons in object ids; BloodHound-reserved property names (objectid, ref) are never emitted.

nodes.label: Shared ID Space Across Inputs
nodes.rationale: CSV and graphify inputs share one ID space in a single run, so a graphify code graph can be enriched with hand-written CSV nodes and edges in one pass.
